summary: This is the Katsumi Degawa Galaxian/Moon Cresta netlist-style core with small ZigZag changes. Address decode is built from 74138/74139 decoder instances and an addressable latch. The video path is a per-pixel scan pipeline of part-numbered registers, an adder, shift registers, a line-buffer counter and a line RAM, all timed from H/V counter bits. ZigZag's second sprite generator is a second copy of that whole pipeline running alongside the first. MAME instead loops over sprite generators and draws sprites in reverse to fake line-buffer priority. The only ZigZag-specific additions are the AY latch and the ROM swap, and both are memory-map details any correct core has to share with MAME.

findings.note: Chip selects come from cascaded LOGIC_74XX139/74XX138 instances that carry board part designators. Each output decodes active-low and is gated by MREQn/RDn/WRn/RFSHn. MAME uses a flat address_map with handler functions.
The 7000-7007 control bits (NMI enable, ROM swap, stars, flips) are one 8-bit latch, selected by A2..A0 and written with data bit D0. MAME has a separate *_w handler for each bit.

findings.signal: WAIT and NMI from raster flip-flops
findings.note: WAITn is a flip-flop clocked by the CPU clock, combining H_BL with the video-RAM decode and cleared by V_BLn. NMI is a flip-flop clocked by the edge of VBLANK and cleared by the latch bit. This is board-level bus contention that MAME does not model.

findings.signal: load/strobe pulse generator from H-count bits
findings.note: LDn, CNTRLDn, CNTRCLRn, COLLn, VPLn, OBJDATALn, MLDn and SLDn are decoded from 1H/2H/4H/8H/256H through 74139 instances. There is also a falling-edge flip-flop (5C) and an edge-captured in-range bit (W_4C2_B). These strobes clock the video registers.

findings.signal: per-pixel object pipeline with part-named registers
findings.note: The OBJ RAM is scanned by an address built from H-count bits. The vertical match is the adder VF_CNT+H_POSI==FF (W_3D), latched on edges of the VPLn and OBJDATALn strobes. MAME computes sy=240-(base0-(sprnum<3)) in a C loop and blits with gfx transpen.

Two 8-bit registers modelled on 74LS299 (hold, shift left, shift right, load) serialize the graphics ROM bytes. A 3L mux picks shift direction and the output bit for horizontal flip. This is the hardware way to do flip, where MAME decodes gfx and blits.

The 45T counter loads the sprite X position and counts at the pixel clock to address a 256x5 line RAM. A pixel is written only where the RAM holds zero (W_VID <= W_RV when W_RV /= "00"), and the 4..7 address bits gate the clip. MAME says it draws sprites 7..0 in reverse to imitate exactly this; the core builds the buffer itself.

findings.signal: second sprite generator duplicated as hardware
findings.note: MAME loops twice over sprites_draw with a 0x20 offset into spriteram. The core instead builds a whole second pipeline (its own LD_PLS, OBJ RAM fed with A xor 0x20, shift registers, counter and line RAM) running in parallel. Its line-buffer output merges with the first generator's per pixel.

findings.signal: raster counter chain and sync/blank from count bits
findings.note: The H counter runs 0-255 then 384-511 (the 256H bit is used as blank), and the V counter is clocked by H_SYNC. HSYNC is a flip-flop on 16H gated by 256H, and C_BLn = V_BLn and not 256H. All of this follows the board's counter-chain wrap behaviour.

The PSG uses the address bus as data: A8 latches A7..0, A0 is the write strobe and A1 is BC. ROM 2/3 swap is A12 xor (swap and A13). Both match MAME's semantics closely but are written as plain equations rather than chips. This is a register map both sides must share.
A 32-byte PROM, addressed by color & 2-bit pixel and split into R3/G3/B2, is the board's palette. MAME's palette init must decode the same PROM.
